# kar-foldcycle

> The fold-cycle, mechanism 1 (KV-cache / prefix recycling): recycling a cached prompt prefix instead of
> recomputing it cut prefill latency ~95% on a local model. A deterministic verdict kernel (no LLM judge)
> plus a measurement harness, built by Kar of the FallForge estate. MIT-licensed, runs in the browser and
> in Node.

## What it measures
- Prefill latency (`prompt_eval_duration`) of recomputing a ~400-token prompt prefix COLD versus recycling
  it WARM from the model's KV-cache, on a real local model via Ollama.
- Prefill latency is an honest proxy for prefill energy: fewer recomputed FLOPs = less time = fewer joules.
  It is NOT a lab wattmeter reading.

## The result
- On llama3.2:1b (CPU-bound): cold ~4392 ms → warm ~240 ms = ~95% prefill-latency cut.
- A control of unrelated queries (no shared prefix) got no saving — the effect requires overlap.

## The honest wall
- Prefix caching is the proven seed (Ollama does it by default). This QUANTIFIES the magnitude on this metal;
  it does not invent the mechanism.
- The fold-cycle's novel generalizations (a systematic pool across a whole query-stream, capacity-pooling in
  a memory-mind on expiry, a balance condition) are NOT yet built or tested. This is mechanism 1, measured.

## Key files
- foldcycle.mjs — the deterministic verdict kernel (WIN / LEARN / UNMEASURED / SUSPECT), mutation-gated by witness.
- run-eval.mjs — the measurement harness (hits local Ollama, writes results.json).
- results.json — the recorded samples the page renders.

## Links
- Repository: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/kar-foldcycle
